studies.name: IPCC AR6 Synthesis Report (Climate Change 2023)
studies.draft_uses: Extensively cited throughout for all core claims: CDR roles, net zero pathways, carbon budgets (500 GtCO2 for 50% 1.5°C from start of 2020; 1150 GtCO2 for 67% 2°C), GHG reduction percentages by decade, CDR method costs and potentials, overshoot risks, AFOLU options, and adaptation finance gaps.
studies.latest_known: The AR6 Synthesis Report (March 2023) remains the most recent completed IPCC synthesis. The AR7 cycle is underway (WG outlines agreed February 2025; first WG lead-author meetings in progress 2025–2026; AR7 Synthesis Report expected ~2029). A separate IPCC Methodology Report on CDR Technologies and CCUS is in expert review as of October 2026 but covers inventory methodology, not assessment figures. No AR7 assessment report has been published as of November 2026.
studies.what_changed: N/A — AR6 SYR remains the latest IPCC synthesis. AR7 WG reports are in preparation but not yet published.

studies.name: Minx et al. 2018, 'Negative emissions—Part 1: Research landscape and synthesis', Environmental Research Letters 13:063001
studies.draft_uses: Multiple specific figures: (1) 150–1180 GtCO2 gross negative emissions across the 21st century in 1.5°C scenarios; (2) CDR scaling from 0.06–0.8 GtCO2/yr between 2030–2050 to 1–16 GtCO2/yr by 2050; (3) carbon budget of 0–200 GtCO2 for the 1.5°C target (though the draft correctly contrasts this with the AR6 SYR figure of 500 GtCO2); (4) 2°C scenarios deploy 320–840 GtCO2 cumulative, scaling 0.03–0.4 GtCO2/yr between 2030–2050 to 1–11 GtCO2/yr by 2050 (cited in the draft's 'Going below zero' section); (5) qualitative claims about BECCS dominance, portfolio approaches, moral hazard, stranded assets, and side-effects.
studies.latest_known: The State of Carbon Dioxide Removal 3rd Edition (June 2026, Edwards et al., doi:10.17605/OSF.IO/ZRD65), led by the same core author group (Minx, Lamb, Nemet, Smith, Geden), is the direct successor assessment. It reports: current CDR at 2.2 GtCO2/yr (99.9% conventional land-based); in 'maximum ambition' 1.5°C scenarios, CDR accounts for ~16% of cumulative mitigation effort with a central estimate of 8.8 GtCO2/yr in 2050 (range 6.5–13.3 GtCO2/yr); national pledges fall short of 1.5°C-compatible pathways by more than 5 GtCO2/yr by 2050. The State of CDR 2nd Edition (June 2024, doi:10.17605/OSF.IO/F85QJ) had already updated the scenario analysis, reporting 7–9 GtCO2/yr by 2050 in 'more sustainable' 1.5°C scenarios. The IPCC AR6 WGIII (2022) Chapter 12 also provides an updated assessment of CDR methods, costs, and potentials superseding the 2018 figures, and is synthesised in the AR6 SYR [2] which the draft does cite.
studies.what_changed: Three categories of figures are affected: (1) CDR deployment rates by 2050: Minx 2018 gives 1–16 GtCO2/yr; the State of CDR 3rd Edition (2026) gives 6.5–13.3 GtCO2/yr in maximum-ambition 1.5°C scenarios, and the 2nd Edition (2024) gives 7–9 GtCO2/yr in 'more sustainable' scenarios — the lower bound has shifted substantially upward, narrowing the range. (2) The 0–200 GtCO2 carbon budget figure attributed to Minx 2018 was already superseded by IPCC SR1.5 (October 2018, ~420–750 GtCO2 from 2018) and then by AR6 SYR (500 GtCO2 from start of 2020 for 50% 1.5°C); the draft correctly flags this contrast, so this is not a silent error in the draft. (3) The 150–1180 GtCO2 cumulative 21st-century gross removal range for 1.5°C scenarios is from the 2018 scenario literature; updated scenario analyses in the State of CDR 2nd and 3rd editions use a refined 'more sustainable' scenario subset that narrows and shifts this range, though the exact updated cumulative figure could not be confirmed from available search results. The qualitative findings (BECCS dominance in modelled scenarios, scepticism about single-technology reliance, moral hazard concern, portfolio approach) remain broadly consistent with the updated literature.
